title: Studying with Aaron Copland
summary: His mother found Copland for him; Copland only asked for melodies and gave his opinions, so Handy wrote them on the train to lessons.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Learning your horn: teachers, lessons and fees

blocks.x: How did you meet Copland?
Through my mother. She found him for me.
Did he have a number of students in those days?
He was teaching. I
He was not then the great man that he is now?

He was known to be a great composer in those days, but I don't think he was very secure financially. Of course I only judge by where he was living, where he was teaching, the kind of surroundings he had. Even that was not a good experience. He didn't give me anything but opinions.
Do you remember the first day you confronted him, the day you met him and talked about why you were there? Do you recall any of those conversations?

No, I don't. I was pretty much still being guided by my family, by my mother and father. With all my resentments, fightings against, I still didn't realize that I could guide myself if I wanted to, or that's all I had left, to go searching my own way.
In those days I was still being controlled and accepting it.
Did you have hope each time that it was going to be different?
With Copland?
With Copland or any of them; did you think this was going to be a good experience?
I always had those hopes but as you said, I began to recognize a pattern that perhaps going to an individual or to an institution to be taught those things wasn't the way.
How did you work with him, or how did he work with you?

He would ask me to write melodies; that's all he ever asked me to do during the period of time I was with him, and I would play them to him, I think the first week that I went to him I may have worked everyday trying to write stuff for him, then I came in and he liked this and he didn't like that and why didn't I

take this and develop it up a little higher and bring it higher and I said because I felt that it was going lower and lower. I couldn't appreciate this kind of-- that wasn't teaching, he wasn't telling me anything. He was telling me his likes and dislikes.
He never told you anything--
About me. He was telling me about Aaron Copland.

So I got so that I would do my work for him on the train ride up to his studio. I wouldn't work at all all week, I played ball and on the day of the lesson I'd get on the train, take out the manuscript paper and the pencil and write fifty melodies on the way up.
He liked some of those melodies, presumably?
He liked some of them.
Was that the way he worked, that was his teaching method?
I couldn't really believe--I think he didn't take me seriously and I didn't take him seriously at all.
